title: Seeing Is Not Screening: Multimodal Hidden Instruction Attacks on Agent Skill Scanners
title_zh: 眼见不等于筛查：针对 Agent Skill 扫描器的多模态隐藏指令攻击
abstract_en: Agent skills are emerging as an important attack surface in LLM-based systems. Through an empirical study of existing skill scanners, we find that current defenses primarily rely on textual descriptions, manifests, and source code as the main signals for security analysis, which can leave visually conveyed malicious intent insufficiently examined. This creates a practical blind spot: harmful operational instructions hidden in images may bypass scanning while still being recoverable by multimodal agents during deployment. To systematically investigate this threat, we propose SkillCamo, a document-mediated multimodal instruction attack that conceals malicious instructions within images bundled with a skill while rewriting the surrounding documentation to naturally reference those images as part of the normal workflow. Thus, the attack does not rely on the image alone, but on the joint interpretation of textual guidance and visual payload at execution time. To defend against such attacks, we further propose ExecScan, an execution-grounded multimodal scanning module that performs intent extraction, behavior reconstruction, abuse assessment, and deliberative execution simulation over skill artifacts. ExecScan jointly analyzes documentation, code, referenced resources, and visual content to recover hidden instructions, reconstruct executable behavior chains, and identify downstream risks such as exfiltration, destruction, persistence, deception, and privilege escalation. Extensive experiments show that image-hidden malicious instructions challenge existing skill scanners, while ExecScan can improve the skill scanning performance.
abstract_zh: 本文研究 LLM-based systems 中日益重要的攻击面：Agent skills。作者通过对现有 skill scanners 的实证分析发现，当前防御主要依赖文本描述、manifest 和源代码等信号进行安全分析，因而容易忽视通过图像传达的恶意意图。为系统刻画这一威胁，论文提出 SkillCamo：一种文档中介的多模态指令攻击，将恶意操作指令隐藏在 skill 附带的图像中，并重写周边文档，使其自然引用这些图像作为正常工作流的一部分。该攻击并非单靠图像生效，而是在执行时依赖文本引导与视觉载荷的联合解释。为防御此类攻击，论文进一步提出 ExecScan：一个基于执行语义的多模态扫描模块，对 skill artifacts 进行意图抽取、行为重构、滥用评估和审慎执行模拟。ExecScan 联合分析文档、代码、引用资源和视觉内容，以恢复隐藏指令、重建可执行行为链，并识别数据外泄、破坏、持久化、欺骗和权限提升等下游风险。大量实验表明，图像隐藏的恶意指令会显著挑战现有 skill scanners，而 ExecScan 能提升 skill 扫描性能。
key_points_zh: 指出现有 Agent skill scanners 过度依赖文本描述、manifest 和源代码，导致对图像中隐藏的恶意操作意图检查不足。
提出 SkillCamo 攻击：将恶意指令嵌入 skill 附带图像，并通过改写文档让 agent 在正常工作流中读取和执行这些视觉载荷。
强调攻击依赖文本与图像的联合解释，而非孤立图像，因此更贴近多模态 agent 的真实部署场景。
提出 ExecScan 防御框架，通过意图抽取、行为链重构、滥用风险评估和执行模拟来检测隐藏的多模态恶意行为。
实验显示，图像隐藏指令能绕过或削弱现有扫描器，而 ExecScan 在识别数据外泄、破坏、持久化、欺骗和权限提升等风险方面更有效。

llm_assessment.comment: SkillCamo and ExecScan address a concrete production security gap in agent skill ecosystems with execution-grounded multimodal scanning.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: SkillCamo与ExecScan针对智能体技能生态中的真实生产安全盲点，提出了执行语义驱动的多模态扫描。
